newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairies saw frost, little precipitation.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairies saw frost, little precipitation.

text.p: Canada's Prairies on Thursday saw overnight lows as cold as -7 Celsius (19.4 F) in Saskatchewan, where 53 percent of harvest was complete, but only trace amounts of precipitation, Environment Canada said.

"Every station that's reported only had trace amounts of precipitation. There's a big warming trend coming in for Saskatchewan, Manitoba and Alberta for the next five days," meteorologist Karen Dewar said.
The entire Prairie grainbelt except for extreme southern Alberta and extreme southwest Saskatchewan saw a killing frost overnight, Dewar said.
Harvest was stalled for one to three weeks by wet weather.
Alberta's harvest was 50 percent complete, Saskatchewan combined 53 percent of crops and Manitoba had 75 percent of crops in the bin by September 30, provincial reports said.
Alberta was forecast to see warmer temperatures with a few showers and flurries and highs of nine to 20 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see a mix of sun and cloud with highs of three to 10 Celsius.
Manitoba was forecast to see mainly sunny skies with highs of six to 10 Celsius.
